themes: India's coal output was 'quite muted' at 1,036 mt in FY26 as heavy monsoons cut Coal India and Singareni output; captive/commercial mines grew 10% to 210 mt. Overburden removal at CIL, SCCL and private mines was 'on a negative side' (MD). Ministry of Coal sees demand of ~1.5-1.67 bn t by FY30.
Ammonium nitrate and input costs (West Asia conflict, 2026)

Key raw-material prices rose 30-40% (ICICI Direct, Aug-2026); Solar raised prices, and contracts carry rise-and-fall clauses, but pass-through covers ~60% of an increase (MD). In FY22-23 a similar spike lifted revenue 57% and 75% while EBITDA margin fell to ~19%.

Jefferies (Sep-2026): India's domestic defence capex to grow ~16% a year for four years; private firms' share of listed defence revenue rose from 9% (FY23) to 16% (FY26); defence exports to grow ~11% a year to Rs 58,400 cr by FY30.

AR FY26: 'well-documented global shortage of medium and large calibre ammunition, especially 155mm'; demand visibility of 5-7 years as Europe, Asia and the Middle East restock. Solar's defence order book includes ~Rs 11,000 cr of international orders (MOFSL).
Traditional electric detonators banned from Jul-2025, moving the industry to electronic systems; the Explosives Regulation Bill 2025 replaces century-old law with digital licensing and tracking.
Orica, Dyno Nobel, Enaex, EPC earn ~14-20% EBITDA margins and trade at ~6-8x EV/EBITDA (PL, Bloomberg). Solar agreed to buy Omnia (BME) in Sep-2026 for ~8x.

Kalyani group reported to be entering explosives (Nomura question, May-2026); Munitions India (state-owned) shares the Pinaka order; Premier Explosives and others in propellants. Domestic mining tenders are price-led (Coal India buys on tender).

peers.note: No listed Indian peer does both mining explosives and defence at Solar's scale. BEL, HAL and BDL are the state-owned defence majors the market prices defence growth against (BDL makes missiles and is Solar's closest product neighbour); Premier Explosives is the only listed explosives-plus-defence-propellants peer (small). Global explosives peers (Orica, Dyno Nobel, Enaex, EPC, Omnia) are not on file; PL's Bloomberg-based multiples are quoted in the text.

moat: ~26% of India's explosives volume (FY25), the world's largest packaged-explosives maker (MD); plants near mines; emulsifiers, detonator shells, PETN, TNT and RDX made in-house.
Lowest-cost supplier in a tender market.
Explosives need PESO licences; defence products need years of trials; Solar was first private firm to dispatch Pinaka Enhanced Mk-I rockets.
Slows new entrants, does not stop funded ones (Kalyani).
Coal India (10% of revenue) buys by tender; pass-through of input costs covers ~60% of an increase.
Margins in explosives are earned on cost, not price.
No captive ammonium nitrate; FY22-23 spike cut margins to ~19%. Omnia's AN plant would change this in southern Africa only.
Integrated from explosives to rockets and drones; defence revenue Rs 2,634 cr (FY26) from Rs 249 cr (FY22); SDAL 30% pre-tax margin.
The source of the premium, and of the risk.
Plants in 11 countries; international revenue Rs 3,815 cr; but rivals are Orica, Dyno Nobel, Enaex, AEL; Turkey subsidiary ~break-even.
Real growth engine, not a moat.
critiques: The price already assumes years of defence growth: ~62x our FY28E EPS; Kotak's DCF gives Rs 11,200 and ours far less.
Omnia brings ~Rs 11,000-12,000 cr of debt whose interest (Rs 1,000-1,100 cr) roughly cancels Omnia's FY28 profit; margins fall to ~20%.
More than half of revenue (60% in FY26) is billed outside India; most defence growth is exports (our inference from the geography note), which are lumpy and policy-exposed.
Defence order book stood at ~Rs 18,000 cr in Mar-26 and Jun-26: execution is running ahead of new orders.
FY26 cash from operations was Rs 621 cr against Rs 1,737 cr of profit: inventory built for geopolitical risk.
Investor on the May-2026 call; GAM
Domestic explosives grew 3% in FY26 as coal overburden removal fell.
Founder and MD were paid Rs 75 cr in FY26 (+56%), the MD 780x the median employee.
Bull case: defence rises from 27% to ~40% of sales and EPS compounds ~31% a year; Omnia adds up to 25% to FY28 EPS.
